cues: Only attaches to whatever follows it, and moving it moves the meaning.
Only I solved two sums: nobody else did.
I only solved two sums: I did nothing more with them.
I solved only two sums: no more than two.
And a negative adverb at the front causes inversion, the auxiliary jumping before the subject: never have I seen such a crowd; rarely does he miss a class; little did they know.
